applied.problem: "In a real cylinder the pressure falls as the gas expands" is too absolute (cylinders also expand at near-steady pressure, as the lesson's own steady stretches show), and the mean effective pressure is defined over an engine's whole cycle, not one expansion.

An indicator card is a closed loop, so the mid-ordinate rule reads the card's height at each strip, not "the pressure"; an engine's mean effective pressure is the cycle's net work over the swept volume; and in the cited notes k is the adiabatic value of n, not just another letter.

Calls the 200 kPa height of a single expansion "the mean effective pressure" without qualification, though the term is defined over an engine's whole cycle; here it is the steady equivalent pressure for this one stroke.
